title: Fpqc family descent from single-morphism descent (proved source-library tool)
statement: Let $P$ be a property of morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], Zariski local on the target, stable under arbitrary base change, and descending along surjective flat quasi-compact morphisms. Let $f:Z\to T$ and let $\{g_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ generate a covering sieve for the fpqc topology [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For each $i$ let $a_i:Z_i\to Z$ and $b_i:Z_i\to T_i$ form a cartesian square with $f,g_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $P(b_i)$ for all $i$, then $P(f)$.

source.place: Tag 02KP, fpqc case, with Topologies Tag 022E; already proved as AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.of_isPullback_of_ofArrows_mem_fpqcTopology in lean/WeilConjectures/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Fpqc.lean, lines 77-139.

proof.text: On an affine open of T, refine the covering sieve by finitely many flat maps from affine schemes. Their disjoint union is affine and its map p to the affine base is flat, surjective and quasi-compact. This is the affine refinement of an fpqc cover (022E).

Every arrow h in the sieve generated by the g_i factors as k followed by some g_i. Given a cartesian square over h, paste and cancel cartesian squares to exhibit its base-changed morphism as a base change of b_i. Stability under arbitrary base change gives P for this morphism.

Apply the preceding observation to the pullback of f along each component of p. Zariski locality on the target, applied to the open covering by components of the disjoint union, gives P for the pullback along p. Single-morphism descent along the surjective flat quasi-compact p gives P for f over this affine base. Zariski locality on the affine open covering of T then gives P(f). The finite empty union is allowed. These steps are the complete existing source proof; no new Lean statement or unproved dependency is introduced.
